description: The data platform: one canonical state layer and several rebuildable serving layers, not a data lake, a graph database or an AI stack. Six tiers in a build order, a deliberately lean first footprint, and — as load-bearing as the build list — the components that are not to be built until workload evidence demands them, each with the evidence that would admit it.
principle: The early advantage is canonical evidence, temporal state and reproducible corpus builds — not infrastructure sprawl. Every component below is either in the first footprint with a reason, or deferred with the measurement that would change that.

1-object-storage.title: Object storage — immutable evidence
1-object-storage.in_repository: platform/sql/002_evidence.sql indexes the objects; the bytes never enter the database (PLAT-009).

2-canonical.title: PostgreSQL + PostGIS — canonical operational truth
2-canonical.isolation: row-level security, ENABLED and FORCED on every tenant table; application roles NOBYPASSRLS. A privileged role bypasses RLS unless deliberately constrained, and the constraint is checked live (PLAT-001, PLAT-002).
2-canonical.in_repository: platform/sql/001,003,004,005,006; platform/check.mjs; platform/test/rls.test.mjs proves the isolation and demonstrates both bypasses.

3-change.title: Outbox + durable workflows — controlled change
3-change.component: PostgreSQL transactional outbox; Temporal for durable workflows
3-change.why_not_kafka: The outbox row commits in the same transaction as the change it describes. A broker is a second system, and 'write, then publish' has a gap that is eventually hit.
3-change.why_temporal: Workflows resume after failure while retaining execution state; a compilation that died at step 7 of 9 restarts at 7, not at 1.
3-change.in_repository: platform/sql/005_outbox.sql with claim_outbox (SKIP LOCKED) and idempotent mark_published; Temporal is declared here and not yet run.

4-lakehouse.title: Lakehouse — historical analytical state
4-lakehouse.component: Parquet on object storage, Apache Iceberg tables
4-lakehouse.why_iceberg: Snapshots, schema evolution and atomic metadata commits are what make a corpus build reproducible and time travel possible.
4-lakehouse.admit_when: A canonical snapshot export exceeds what PostgreSQL serves analytically at acceptable cost, or a corpus build needs time travel over history PostgreSQL no longer holds live. Measured, not assumed.

5-projections.title: Rebuildable serving projections
5-projections.rule: No serving projection writes canonical truth. Enforced as a permission — the projection role holds no write grant on canonical or evidence (PLAT-004) — not as a convention.

spatial.note: Declared; this development image carries no PostGIS extension, and the checker reports the tier as declared-not-installed rather than pretending.

graph.first: PostgreSQL recursive CTEs and materialized views
graph.admit_next_when: A measured traversal limit — depth, fan-out or latency — that projection.reachable() with its depth cap and cycle guard cannot meet. A graph database is admitted on that measurement, never on its absence.

semantic.first: a versioned vector projection keyed to canonical ids
semantic.admit_when: Measured latency or scale decides between pgvector and Qdrant. Neither is installed until there is a query to measure.

lexical.admit_next_when: Lexical retrieval needs measured to exceed what PostgreSQL provides. A separate search index is admitted on that measurement.

components.kernel references: notation:// names and content digests throughout; canonical.notation_uri is a domain, and evidence.content_hash is checked to be a sha256.
components.manifests: corpus-build and result manifests; projection.build records what was built, from which revision, and the command that rebuilds it.
components.ci: GitLab CI for code, containers, deployment provenance and Harness runs. This repository's own CI is GitHub Actions today; the platform's provenance chain is declared for GitLab and the migration is a footprint change, not a doctrine change.
components.proofs: SP1 proofs for selected deterministic computations — the Scientific Transformer Engine and BIM State Transformer already declare SP1 guests in the catalog.
components.telemetry: OpenTelemetry for traces, metrics and logs across ingestion, compilation, APIs and agents.

deferred.Apache Iceberg: a canonical snapshot export PostgreSQL cannot serve analytically at acceptable cost
deferred.vector search (pgvector or Qdrant): a semantic query to measure; the choice between them is a latency and scale measurement
deferred.graph database: a measured traversal limit projection.reachable() cannot meet
deferred.streaming broker (Kafka): an outbox relay measured to be the bottleneck, not a preference for streaming
deferred.GPU workers: a model workload measured to need them; the catalog's GPU systems run where they run today
deferred.Kubernetes: an operational load that a small number of hosts cannot carry, measured

invariants.PLAT-001: Row security is enabled AND forced on every tenant table. Enabled alone exempts the table owner.
invariants.PLAT-002: No application role holds BYPASSRLS or SUPERUSER.
invariants.PLAT-003: Every table with row security has a policy.
invariants.PLAT-004: No serving projection writes canonical truth: the projection role holds no write grant on canonical or evidence.
invariants.PLAT-005: Canonical and evidence are append-only for the application: no DELETE, UPDATE only on supersession columns.
invariants.PLAT-006: Every canonical fact is bitemporal — event time and knowledge time as separate columns.
invariants.PLAT-007: Every evidence object carries content hash, rights, retention, access scope and source, all NOT NULL.
invariants.PLAT-008: The transactional outbox exists with a partial index on its backlog.
invariants.PLAT-009: Evidence rows describe objects and never hold their bytes.
